description: Equipo conformado por estudiantes de la institución educativa Futura Schools, sede Cerro Colorado - Arequipa
summary: Project Ares is an international mission that explores space, specifically Mars. It aims to explore Mars' history and whether it had the right conditions for life. This will be done by using the fictional ‘Ares Explorer’ rover inspired by NASA’s Opportunity to study Martian rock, mineral and signs of ancient water. Many different countries have contributed to the project such as the USA, Japan, Canada, China, Russia, and India. The biggest debate around Project Ares is whether the rover should be retrieved after completing its mission. There are many factors to consider including how much science can be gained from it, the risks involved and how expensive the mission will be (between 8-11 billion dollars). The countries have proposed to send an international robotic mission to Mars to protect science, create new technology and prepare for future human missions.
details:
1. The Ares Project was inspired by NASA's Opportunity rover. It uses solar panels, cameras, sensors, robotic arms, and special tools to study Martian rocks, minerals, and soil.

2. Our goal is to promote awareness of the scientific importance of Mars rovers, encourage technological innovation, and inspire future generations to explore Mars.

3. Our project inspires young people to become interested in space exploration beyond the Moon. It also shows how new technologies can make future missions safer.

4. We used Lovable to create the website, Gemini AI to collect information, and ChatGPT to write formal texts and APA citations. We also used translation tools to make the English easier to understand.

5. Our project is creative because it presents a fictional international mission inspired by NASA. It combines scientific research, international cooperation, and a debate based on MUNSUR to develop young people's leadership and argumentation skills.

6. We considered economic factors, crew and equipment safety, Mars' extreme conditions, and communication problems. We also studied the rover's scientific and historical importance, robotic retrieval options, and the mission's costs and risks.
